questions.question_text: Regarding testamentary capacity, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The term testamentary capacity is the same as fitness to plead
If someone is suffering from a mental illness at the time of making a will, the will is not legally valid
T o decide that the testator is of sound disposing mind, he or she should know the exact nature and extent of the property, down to thesmallest detail
T o decide that the testator is of sound disposing mind, he or she should know the names of close relatives and should be able to assesstheir claims to the property
T o decide that the testator is of sound disposing mind, he or she should be free from delusional thoughts

correct_answer.text: T o decide that the testator is of sound disposing mind, he or she should know the names of close relatives and should be able to assesstheir claims to the property

correct_answers.text: T o decide that the testator is of sound disposing mind, he or she should know the names of close relatives and should be able to assesstheir claims to the property

questions.explanation: The term 'testamentary capacity' is the capacity to make a valid will. If a person has a mental illness at the time of making a will, its validity may be in doubt and it could be challenged. But the will is still legally valid if the testator is of sound disposing mind. T o make sure that the testator is of sound disposing mind, he or she should know what the will is and its consequences, the nature and extent of the property (not necessarily in detail), and the names of close relatives, and he or she should be able to assess their claims to the property. The testator should not have an abnormal state of mind with distorted judgements affecting capability tomake the will. A deluded person can make a valid will if that delusion does not distort his or her feelings or judgements relevant to making the will.

questions.question_text: A 82-year-old woman admitted to the medical ward after being found unwell at her home by a carer complains to family members visiting her on the ward next day that the staff on the ward are stealing her things and poisoning her food. She appears bemused and bewildered and tells the family that there were hooded men around her bed the previous evening. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Typically the onset of delirium is acute and present in 18% of patients admitted to a geriatric ward and it increases to 24% in the course of their stay. Because of the acute onset, the patient is often perplexed and suspicious, with delusions and visual hallucinations.

questions.question_text: A 48-year-old homeless man is brought to the A&E department in an agitated and confused state by paramedics. He complains of wavering vision and sees double when looking to the side. He needs support on walking and has a disturbed gait. On examination he has nystagmus and conjugate gait paralysis. An MRI scan performed using T2-dependent sequences shows abnormal high-intensity areas surrounding the third ventricles in the massa intermedia, the floor of the third ventricle, the mammillary bodies, the reticular formation and the periaqueductal region. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is Wernicke's encephalopathy, with the characteristic clinical triad of confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia, and radiological findings.

questions.question_text: A 44-year-old man is brought to the A&E department with disinhibition, ataxia and visual disturbances. On CT scan, hypodense areas are visible in the putamen; a T2-weighted MRI study shows high-intensity necrotic areas in the putamen. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: The initial presentation of methanol intoxication is the same as ethanol toxicity. Patients may develop headache, nausea, vomiting or epigastric pain and rapidly progress to obtundation and coma. Oculotoxicity may lead to blindness; neuroimaging reveals characteristic lesions in the putamen as described.

questions.question_text: Immediately after a myocardial infarction, a 58-year-old man develops depression of moderate severity and has some deliberate self-harm ideations, but with no suicidal intentions; the preferred antidepressant of choice is:
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine, paroxetine and citalopram cause a small decrease in heart rate. Lofepramine increases heart rate moderately. With fluoxetine, paroxetine and lofepramine some cases of arrhythmias have been reported. Meta-analysis of controlled trials of SSRIs has found no significant increases in suicidal ideation or suicidal acts, as compared with placebo or tricyclic antidepressants.

questions.question_text: A 42-year-old woman is referred to you with a history of eating excessively and inappropriately after developing herpes encephalitis. There have been some changes in her personality, including increased agitation, and she has gained 12 kg in the last three months. Which of the following explains this presentation?
questions.explanation: Kluver–Bucy syndrome is associated with temporal lobe abnormality. Kleine–Levin syndrome is associated with periodic somnolence and hyperphagia. In both syndromes hypersexuality can occur. Kearns–Sayre syndrome is mitochondrial myopathy.

questions.question_text: Sexual dysfunction associated with SSRIs is mediated mainly by:
questions.explanation: By binding to serotonin, transporter SSRIs block the reuptake of released 5-HT and increase the concentration of 5-HT at its receptors, which are both post- and presynaptic. The 5-HT 1 receptor mediates antidepressant and anxiolytic activity and 5-HT 2 receptor stimulation mediates insomnia, agitation and sexual dysfunction. 5-HT 3 is associated with nausea and headaches.

questions.question_text: NO-synthase inhibition by which of the following SSRIs may contribute to erectile dysfunction?
questions.explanation: Paroxetine, sertraline and citalopram have anticholinergic side-effects; the prolactin level is slightly raised by paroxetine and citalopram but not sertraline.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antipsychotic drugs was shown to be useful in the prophylaxis of delirium?
questions.explanation: Kalisvaart et al. (2005) showed in a randomized placebo-controlled study that low-dose haloperidol prophylactic treatment demonstrated no efficacy in reducing the incidence of postoperative delirium. It did have a positive effect on the severity and duration of delirium. Moreover, haloperidol reduced the number of days patients stayed in the hospital, and the therapy was well tolerated.

questions.question_text: Regarding sexual dysfunction, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Sexual dysfunction in the general population is more prevalent in men
Comparative studies indicate higher levels of sexual dysfunction in patients with depression than in controls
Comparative studies of SSRIs have generally found no significant differences between drugs in causing sexual dysfunction
Maprotiline and moclobemide are less likely to cause sexual dysfunction than amitriptyline and doxepin, respectively
Bupropion and nefazodone are less likely to cause sexual dysfunction than sertraline

correct_answer.text: Sexual dysfunction in the general population is more prevalent in men

correct_answers.text: Sexual dysfunction in the general population is more prevalent in men

questions.explanation: Sexual dysfunction in the general population is more prevalent in women (43%) than men (31%). There are probable advantages: of maprotiline and moclobemide over amitriptyline and doxepin, respectively; of bupropion (amfebutamone) and reboxetine over fluvoxamine; and of bupropion and nefazodone over sertraline.

questions.question_text: In which of the following is the pulvinar sign seen on MRI?
questions.explanation: The pulvinar sign on MRI is hyperintensity over the posterior thalamus (a useful and non-invasive diagnostic sign).

questions.question_text: A 28-year-old man is brought to the A&E department complaining of acute onset of confusion. His relatives report that he has complained of a strange smell that others cannot perceive and has said that there is something churning in his stomach and rising towards his throat. He expresses an intense sense of familiarity with you and your surroundings. He also has flushing and tachycardia. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Complex partial seizure (temporal lobe epilepsy) presents with epigastric aura, autonomic signs and distorted perceptions, including olfactory hallucinations and deja vu phenomena.

questions.question_text: You have seen as an outpatient a 22-year-old man with progressive memory impairment and long-standing extrapyramidal symptoms, including rigidity, dystonia and choreoathetoid movements. His MRI scan was reported to have shown generalized brain atrophy and 'tiger's eye' appearance. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Hallervorden–Spatz syndrome is autosomal recessive and MRI shows destruction of the central part of the globus pallidus, surrounded by dark signal due to iron deposition ('tiger's eye' appearance).

questions.question_text: ICD-10 confirms the diagnosis of enduring personality change after a catastrophic experience if the change has lasted for at least:
questions.explanation: ICD-10 has three categories of change in personality: (1) due to organic disease of the brain classified in section F00; (2) enduring personality change after psychiatric illness; and (3) enduring personality change after a catastrophic experience. (2) and (3) are classified in section F60 and need the change to have lasted for at least 2 years.

questions.question_text: Regarding biological abnormalities in people with personality disorders, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Reduced prefrontal grey matter was observed in people with antisocial personality disorder
Deficits in the amygdala response to emotional stimuli were observed in people with antisocial personality disorder
A decreased volume of amygdala was observed in people with sociopathic personalities
Increased levels of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid have been found in the cerebrospinal fluid of people who have committed unpremeditated violence
5HT -mediated prolactin release is lower in subjects with histories of impulsive aggressiveness

correct_answer.text: Increased levels of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid have been found in the cerebrospinal fluid of people who have committed unpremeditated violence

correct_answers.text: Increased levels of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid have been found in the cerebrospinal fluid of people who have committed unpremeditated violence

questions.explanation: Low levels of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid have been found in the cerebrospinal fluid of people who have committed unpremeditated violence.

questions.question_text: Contraindications of zopiclone include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: As zopiclone can cause respiratory depression, muscle weakness and stable myasthenia gravis, caution is advised.

questions.question_text: Bilateral concentric visual field defects have been reported in patients treated with:
questions.explanation: The visual field defects associated with vigabatrin start from 1 month to several years after beginning treatment. In most cases the defects persist after discontinuation. Visual field testing before treatment is advised.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old farmer referred by his GP to your outpatient department presents with a history of fatigue and low motivation for the last few weeks as well as arthritic pain on multiple joints. He appears low in mood and tells you that he has a rash on his chest, which is extending slowly. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Lyme disease is caused by the spirochaete Borrelia burgdorferi, which is transmitted to humans through tick bites. The tick bite is followed by the rash erythema migrans, a spreading annular erythema extending slowly outwards on the trunk or limbs, which is often a pointer to the diagnosis. Lyme disease is associated with neuropsychological problems and systemic disturbances.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding chronic fatigue syndrome are true, except:

options.text: Estimate of prevalence is between 0.3% and 1.5% of the general population
The diagnosis requires that the illness must have lasted for at least 6 months
It is associated with tender lymph nodes
SSRIs are the treatment of choice, with proven efficacy

correct_answer.text: SSRIs are the treatment of choice, with proven efficacy

correct_answers.text: SSRIs are the treatment of choice, with proven efficacy

questions.explanation: Many treatments have been suggested but very few are of proven efficacy. Cognitive behavioural therapy and graded exercise regimes have shown some benefits over standard medical care alone. Whenthere is definite evidence of depressive disorder, antidepressants should be prescribed; SSRIs are better tolerated. Antidepressants are also useful in reducing anxiety, improving sleep and reducing pain.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding fibromyalgia are true, except:

options.text: It is often accompanied by poor sleep, muscle aching and tenderness at trigger points
The arms and legs are affected more than other parts of the body
It is more common in women
It is more common in middle age
Controlled trials have shown the value of antidepressants

correct_answer.text: The arms and legs are affected more than other parts of the body

correct_answers.text: The arms and legs are affected more than other parts of the body

questions.explanation: The cervical and thoracic areas are affected most often but the pins may be located in the arms and legs. There is a marked association with depression and anxiety.

questions.question_text: Regarding somatic symptoms unexplained by somatic pathology, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: When the diagnosis of factitious disorder, including the findings and their implications, is explained to patients, some admit that the symptoms are self-inflicted
The majority of people with irritable bowel syndrome consult a doctor
People with Munchausen syndrome usually encourage health professionals to obtain information about their previous treatments from other hospitals
In factitious disorder by proxy, gastrointestinal signs are most commonly reported
Malingering is not usually for the purpose of obtaining any gain

correct_answer.text: When the diagnosis of factitious disorder, including the findings and their implications, is explained to patients, some admit that the symptoms are self-inflicted

correct_answers.text: When the diagnosis of factitious disorder, including the findings and their implications, is explained to patients, some admit that the symptoms are self-inflicted

questions.explanation: Irritable bowel syndrome occurs in as many as 10% of the general population, the majority of whom do not consult a doctor. People with Munchausen syndrome usually obstruct health professionals from obtaining information about their previous treatments from other hospitals. In factitious disorder by proxy, the signs reported most commonly are neurological, bleeding and rashes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about factitious disorder by proxy is true?

options.text: Some children collude in the production of symptoms and signs
Perpetrators usually have severe personality disorders and some may have a factitious disorder
The prognosis is poor for children
The prognosis is poor for perpetrators

questions.explanation: Hazards for children include disruption of education and social development. Occasional cases of murder are also reported.

questions.question_text: A 34-year-old woman recently diagnosed with multiple sclerosis is developing increasingly severe depressive symptoms after starting treatment. The most probable pharmacological reason for this is treatment with:
questions.explanation: Depression is a side-effect of beta interferon therapy and it is advised that it should not be used in people with severe depressive illness and suicidal ideation.

questions.question_text: People with emotionally unstable personality disorder (borderline type) are believed to be operating in:
questions.explanation: The paranoid-schizoid position is characterized by the predominance of primitive defence mechanisms, i.e. denial, splitting and primitive projective identification in the more mature depressive position. There isintegration of good and bad aspects of self and others. Most people with borderline personalities operate more in the paranoid-schizoid than in the depressive position.

questions.question_text: You are asked to assess a 24-year-old man who has been brought to your unit by the police. The police report that he has been involved in several violent crimes. In front of you he appears calm and knowledgeable about psychiatric problems and tells you that the police officers did not do their job properly as they did not arrest the people he was fighting with. When the police officer tries to interrupt him he suddenly becomes violent and kicks the officer. You have a discussion with his mother over the phone and she tells you that her son has had conduct disorder in the past and has low tolerance to frustration and a low threshold for aggression and violence. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Callous unconcern for the feelings of others, superficial charm, persistent disregard for social norms, low capacity for maintaining personal relationships, conduct disorder in childhood, low tolerance to frustration and low threshold for aggression and violence are all features of antisocial personality disorder.

questions.question_text: Diagnostic criteria for borderline personality disorder include all of the following, except:

options.text: Disturbance in and uncertainty about self-image, aims and internal preferences (including sexual)
Liability to become involved in intense and unstable relationships, often leading to emotional crisis
Recurrent threats or acts of self-harm
Chronic feeling of low mood and depression

correct_answer.text: Chronic feeling of low mood and depression

correct_answers.text: Chronic feeling of low mood and depression

questions.explanation: ICD-10 requires a chronic feeling of emptiness (not low mood and depression).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is least recommended in the management of antisocial personality disorder?

options.text: Problem-solving counselling to help the patient deal with stressful circumstances that provoke abnormal behaviour or painful feelings
Psychodynamic counselling to help the patient deal with stressful circumstances that provoke abnormal behaviour or painful feelings
Antipsychotic drugs to calm the aggressive behaviour arising in response to increased stress
Antidepressant medications to control the depressive symptoms associated with increased stress
Anxiolytic drugs to control the mood and anxiety symptoms associated with increased stress

correct_answer.text: Anxiolytic drugs to control the mood and anxiety symptoms associated with increased stress

correct_answers.text: Anxiolytic drugs to control the mood and anxiety symptoms associated with increased stress

questions.explanation: Anxiolytic drugs should be avoided as they may cause disinhibition and dependency.

questions.question_text: Obsessive compulsive disorder can be associated with:

options.text: Gilles de la T ourette syndrome

questions.explanation: Obsessive compulsive disorder is found in association with many organic brain diseases, including epilepsy and encephalitis lethargica.

questions.question_text: In severe obsessive compulsive disorder with obsessional rituals, the most appropriate treatment is:

options.text: Exposure and response prevention with SSRIs

correct_answer.text: Exposure and response prevention with SSRIs

correct_answers.text: Exposure and response prevention with SSRIs

questions.explanation: Exposure and response prevention seem to produce better long-term results but it is difficult to achieve response prevention when symptoms are severe. For this reason, medication and response prevention should often be combined. Obsessional rituals usually respond very well to exposure and response prevention.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about social phobia are true, except:

options.text: Patients are often preoccupied with the idea of being observed critically
It is a predictor of alcohol misuse
Suicide attempts are more frequent than in the general population
Positron emission tomography (PET) study of social phobics experiencing anticipatory anxiety found decreased blood flow in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
Successful treatment with citalopram or cognitive behavioural therapy results in decreased blood flow in the amygdala and related brain areas

correct_answer.text: Positron emission tomography (PET) study of social phobics experiencing anticipatory anxiety found decreased blood flow in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex

correct_answers.text: Positron emission tomography (PET) study of social phobics experiencing anticipatory anxiety found decreased blood flow in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex

questions.explanation: A PET study of social phobics experiencing anticipatory anxiety found increased blood flow in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, left inferior temporal cortex and left amygdaloid–hippocampal region.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the psychological treatment of choice for social phobia?
questions.explanation: A modified form of cognitive behavioural therapy based on particular cognitive abnormalities, coupled with measures to reduce safety behaviours, using video and audio feedback, was found to be more effective.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) are true, except:

options.text: Social phobia is the most common comorbid anxiety disorder occurring with GAD
DSM-IV allows the diagnosis of mixed anxiety and depressive disorder
Phaeochromocytoma and hypoglycaemia should be considered in the differential diagnosis of GAD
Lifetime prevalence of GAD is around 5%, with women affected more than men
Anxiety disorders lasting for more than 6 months have a poor prognosis

correct_answer.text: DSM-IV allows the diagnosis of mixed anxiety and depressive disorder

correct_answers.text: DSM-IV allows the diagnosis of mixed anxiety and depressive disorder

questions.explanation: ICD-10 allows the diagnosis of mixed anxiety and depressive disorder, but in DSM-IV there is a need for both diagnoses if they occur together.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding primary depersonalization disorder, except:

options.text: It is classified as a dissociative disorder in DSM-IV
It is characteristically experienced as an unpleasant state by the patient
It is possibly associated with schizoid personality disorder
It is associated with a greater response in the insula and occipitotemporal cortex in an fMRI study
In the majority of people depersonalization does not persist for a long time

correct_answer.text: It is associated with a greater response in the insula and occipitotemporal cortex in an fMRI study

correct_answers.text: It is associated with a greater response in the insula and occipitotemporal cortex in an fMRI study

questions.explanation: Primary depersonalization disorder is rare and is associated with a smaller response in the insula and occipitotemporal cortex in fMRI study and a greater response in the right ventral prefrontal cortex.

questions.question_text: In DSM-IV, the diagnosis of acute stress disorder requires: marked symptoms of anxiety or increased arousal; re-experiencing of the distressing event; and three dissociative symptoms from a list of five. All of the following are included in those dissociative symptoms, except:

options.text: A sense of numbing or detachment

questions.explanation: Reduced awareness of the surroundings and being in a daze is the dissociative symptom.

questions.question_text: All of the following are individual factors that increase vulnerability to the development of post-traumatic stress disorder, except:
questions.explanation: Factors summarized by Ozer et al. (2003) include lower intelligence and personal history of mood and anxiety disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a neurobiological abnormality in post-traumatic stress disorder?

options.text: Increased levels of corticotropin-releasing hormone in the cerebrospinal fluid

questions.explanation: All these are found to be associated with abnormalities in the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis mediating defensive responses to stressful events, and there is a general increase in lability following environmental stress.

questions.question_text: Regarding the involvement of the monoamine neurotransmitter noradrenaline in the neurobiology of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Sympathetic tone is increased in PTSD
Startle response is increased in PTSD
MHPG level is decreased in the cerebrospinal fluid
There is an increased anxiety response to noradrenaline challenge
There is increased activity in noradrenergic innervation of the amygdala

correct_answer.text: MHPG level is decreased in the cerebrospinal fluid

correct_answers.text: MHPG level is decreased in the cerebrospinal fluid

questions.explanation: MHPG level is increased in the cerebrospinal fluid. The increased activity in noradrenergic innervation of the amygdala increases arousal and facilitates the automatic encoding and recall of traumatic memories.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man presents as an outpatient with a history of anxiety, some insomnia and poor concentration after a car accident 3 weeks previously. He has had flashbacks and a few distressing dreams relating to the accident. The most appropriate management option is:

options.text: A critical incident debriefing (CID) and discharge back to the GP for primary-care follow-up
Watchful waiting and a follow-up appointment within a month
Short-term anxiolytic medication and urgent referral for trauma-focused cognitive behavioural treatment
Eye movement and desensitization reprocessing therapy
Citalopram to be started on 10 mg/day, with a view to increasing it in 3 weeks' time to 20 mg if there are no side-effects, and a follow-up appointment in 6 weeks

correct_answer.text: Watchful waiting and a follow-up appointment within a month

correct_answers.text: Watchful waiting and a follow-up appointment within a month

questions.explanation: According to guidance from the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) on the management of post-traumatic stress disorder and related traumatic syndromes, where symptoms are mild and have been present for less than 4 weeks after the trauma, watchful waiting and a follow-up appointment within a month are recommended.

questions.question_text: A 44-year-old man who lives with his wife comes to your outpatient clinic. He has appeared low in mood for the past 9 months since his mother's sudden and unexpected death. He wakes up early in the morning and sometimes hears his mother's voice calling him. Although he has had some thoughts about joining his mother in heaven he does not want to end his life. His wife says that he drinks a few days a week to get rid of the difficult thoughts from his head. In your assessment he meets the criteria for a depressive disorder of moderate severity. The most appropriate management plan is:

options.text: Admission to the inpatient ward and treatment with antipsychotic medication

questions.explanation: Antidepressants are beneficial if criteria for depressive disorders are met.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about atypical depression are true, except:

options.text: Variably depressed mood with mood reactivity to positive events occurs
Extreme fatigue and heaviness in the limbs are features
There is a better response to tricyclic antidepressants than to MAOIs and SSRIs

correct_answer.text: There is a better response to tricyclic antidepressants than to MAOIs and SSRIs

correct_answers.text: There is a better response to tricyclic antidepressants than to MAOIs and SSRIs

questions.explanation: There is a better response to MAOIs and SSRIs and a poorer response to tricyclic antidepressants.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about rapid cycling disorder, except:

options.text: There should be at least four episodes a year separated by a period of remission or a switch to an episode of opposite polarity
It occurs more frequently in women
It can be triggered by antidepressant treatment
Lithium is the most effective treatment as a mood stabilizer

correct_answer.text: Lithium is the most effective treatment as a mood stabilizer

correct_answers.text: Lithium is the most effective treatment as a mood stabilizer

questions.explanation: Lithium treatment is relatively ineffective.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding seasonal affective disorder?

options.text: Onset occurs in autumn or winter and recovery in spring or summer
Increased appetite with a craving for carbohydrate occurs
An afternoon slump in energy is a feature

questions.explanation: It was suggested that shortening of daylight hours is important in pathophysiology; exposure to bright artificial light during hours of darkness is used as treatment.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about mood disorders are true, except:

options.text: The point prevalence of depression is greater than that of bipolar illness
The mean age of onset is 10 years later in depression than in bipolar illness
The risk of mood disorders is about twice as great in first-degree relatives of bipolar patients
The prevalence of depression and bipolar illness is twice as great in women as men
It has been estimated that 10% of patients presenting with a depressive disorder will eventually have a manic illness

correct_answer.text: The prevalence of depression and bipolar illness is twice as great in women as men

correct_answers.text: The prevalence of depression and bipolar illness is twice as great in women as men

questions.explanation: The prevalence of bipolar illness in men and women is the same; the rates of major depression are about twice as great in women as in men; the lifetime risk of bipolar disorder is between 0.3% and 1.5%; the 5- and 6-month prevalence is not much less than the lifetime prevalence as the illness is chronic. Mean age of onset for bipolar illness is 17 and that of depression is 27.

questions.question_text: Abnormalities in monoamine neurotransmission in depression include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Overall research evidence does not suggest that drug-free patients with major depression have a consistent reduction in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA).

questions.question_text: Regarding neurochemical abnormalities of depression, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Drug-free patients with major depression have a consistent reduction in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA)
Blunted noradrenaline-mediated growth hormone release is seen in depression
Clinical relapse of depression occurs after administration of AMPT
Decreased homovanillic acid (HVA) levels in the cerebrospinal fluid is seen in depression
Increased dopamine D2 receptor binding occurs in depression

correct_answer.text: Drug-free patients with major depression have a consistent reduction in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA)

correct_answers.text: Drug-free patients with major depression have a consistent reduction in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA)

questions.explanation: Increased dopamine D2 receptor binding occurs in depression.

questions.question_text: Low CSF 5-HIAA levels in patients who have made impulsive and more dangerous suicide attempts are observed in:
questions.explanation: It has been proposed that low levels of CSF 5-HIAA, while not related specifically to depression, may be associated with a tendency for individuals to respond in an impulsive and hostile way to life difficulties.

questions.question_text: About half of patients suffer from depression in which of the following?
questions.explanation: In Cushing syndrome, depression usually remits when cortisol hypersecretion is corrected.

questions.question_text: Blunted thyrotropin-stimulating hormone (TSH) response to intravenous thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) is seen in all the following conditions, except:
questions.explanation: Normal thyrotropin-stimulating hormone (TSH) response to intravenous thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) is observed in schizophrenia. It is also observed that in schizophrenia there is a blunted release of prolactin and growth hormone on thyroid-releasing hormonestimulation.

questions.question_text: Immune changes in depression include which of the following?

options.text: Lowered proliferative responses of lymphocytes to mitogens

questions.explanation: Cytokines are known to provoke hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis activity and therefore changes in immunoregulation may play a part in HPA axis dysfunction in depression.

questions.question_text: Sleep changes in depression include which of the following?

options.text: Increase in the proportion of REM sleep in the early part of the night

questions.explanation: Decreased REM sleep latency may persist in recovered depressed patients and indicate a vulnerability to relapse.
